allusions.nt_words: καὶ προσκυνησάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες ἄγγελοι θεοῦ
allusions.ot_mt_form: MT Deut 32:43 lacks any reference to angels worshiping; reads 'Rejoice, O nations, with his people' (הרנינו גוים עמו) — significantly shorter than LXX
allusions.ot_lxx_form: LXX Deut 32:43: καὶ προσκυνησάτωσαν αὐτῷ πάντες υἱοὶ θεοῦ ('let all the sons of God worship him'); a variant LXX/Odes 2:43 tradition reads πάντες ἄγγελοι θεοῦ
allusions.textual_implication: The citation has no parallel in the MT of Deut 32:43, which is shorter; it depends on the longer LXX form (now confirmed by 4QDeut^q, which preserves a Hebrew Vorlage with 'bow down to him, all gods/sons of God'). Hebrews' exact wording 'ἄγγελοι θεοῦ' matches Odes 2:43 and a strand of LXX manuscripts (rather than the majority LXX 'υἱοὶ θεοῦ'), suggesting the author used a liturgical/recensional form. The author applies a verse about YHWH's vindication to the enthronement of the Son, presupposing a Greek Bible.
allusions.textual_implication_plain: Hebrews quotes a longer Greek version of Deuteronomy 32:43 that the standard Hebrew Bible does not contain — a version where angels worship God. The Dead Sea Scrolls show this longer reading really existed in Hebrew too, so the Greek translators weren't inventing it.
allusions.scholarly_note: Beale & Carson (Commentary, ad loc., G. Guthrie) and most commentators (Attridge, Ellingworth) identify Deut 32:43 LXX as primary, though some (Bateman) argue for Ps 97:7 LXX; the wording 'ἄγγελοι' over 'υἱοὶ' aligns Hebrews with Odes 2.

summary_technical: Hebrews 1:6 cites a form of Deut 32:43 available only in the LXX tradition (specifically the Odes/recensional reading with ἄγγελοι θεοῦ), with no equivalent in the MT but partial confirmation in 4QDeut^q. The citation exemplifies the author's consistent dependence on a Greek Vorlage and his christological repurposing of theophanic Yahweh-texts.
summary_plain: Hebrews quotes a Greek version of Deuteronomy that calls angels to worship God, and applies it to Jesus — a verse missing from the standard Hebrew Bible.

bibcrit_hypothesis.title: Odes-form Deuteronomy 32 in Hebrews' Vorlage
bibcrit_hypothesis.reasoning: The precise wording ἄγγελοι θεοῦ (not the majority-LXX υἱοὶ θεοῦ) suggests the author of Hebrews drew on a liturgical collection resembling Odes 2 rather than a continuous Pentateuch scroll. This fits the catena structure of Hebrews 1, where OT texts appear pre-selected for christological enthronement themes. The 4QDeut^q evidence shows the longer reading was not a Christian interpolation but reflects a genuine pre-Christian Hebrew variant preserved in Greek liturgy.
bibcrit_hypothesis.plain: The author of Hebrews probably knew Deuteronomy 32 from a hymn-book or liturgy used in synagogue worship, not from a standard Bible scroll. That explains why his quotation matches the wording of an early Christian/Jewish hymnal more than the main Greek Bible.
